lines.text: Some Herkimer diamonds hold hardened petroleum.

post.caption: Some Herkimer diamonds hold hardened petroleum. Herkimer diamonds are really clear quartz crystals, and each crystal has a point at both ends. They grew freely in rock cavities, so both ends could form, and the rock around them is about 500 million years old. Quartz is about 7 on the Mohs scale, while diamond is 10, and many form with 18 natural facets. The name comes from their clarity and well-formed faces. Some hold black specks of anthraxolite, which is hardened petroleum, and others hold tiny pockets of water or petroleum. At one New York mine, visitors can dig and keep their finds.
